clues: This city lies in the center of a wide river valley, beside a broad river that flows north. Low green hills ring the town on three sides.
Rain pours down in late fall and winter here, under grey skies for weeks. Then summer turns bone dry, with scarce a drop for month after month.
This town became the land's capital in 1851, just nine years after its start. It lost the role for a few months in 1855, then won it back for good.
In 1840 the first lasting settlers built a mission in this green river valley. Farms and orchards soon spread across the rich flat land around it.
Oregon law men meet in this city, in the state capitol. A gold statue of a first settler tops this third hall.
